notes.summary: All-field primary mixed-multiplicity kernel on reduced excellent germs, including unused labels, integral-closure invariance and monotonicity on the same superficial quotients.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves every power/product law, function-order compatibility, integral-closure invariance, exact-sequence top-form additivity and mixed monotonicity. The algebraic extension R(z) preserves lengths and dimensions. Superficial quotients may be nonreduced, embedded and nonpure. Uses the qualified G331 boundary and valuative criterion, with disclosed ordinary published Hilbert and superficial-element dependencies.
notes.text:
Let R be the reduction of an excellent local ring, n=dim R>=1, and a a proper primary ideal. Use the entire G331 normalized boundary X_a, retaining every support. G331 supplies the independently geometric continuous class C, its comparison with the uniform ideal closure, and its actual decreasing-net completion D. It supplies no operator.

All multiplicities use degree n of the REDUCED ring. Smaller-dimensional modules contribute zero. A positive-dimensional local ring has no zero-dimensional minimal component: its maximal ideal cannot be minimal while a smaller prime exists. Thus G331's zero-dimensional minimal-component exception does not arise in the primary criterion here. Auxiliary superficial quotients can be nonreduced and have embedded primes.

The complete current Swanson–Huneke 17.4.2 and Definition 17.4.3 give the eventual polynomial length(M/I1^s1...Ir^sr M), of degree dim M. Its degree-n form is H(s)=sum_{|d|=n} e(I1^[d1],...,Ir^[dr];M)s^d/(d1!...dr!). With n separately labelled entries, e(I1,...,In) is the coefficient of s1...sn. Repeated equal labels recover ordinary multiplicity by substituting the sum of their variables. A unit label contributes no variable dependence.

Unused labels need a separate argument. Fix the unused primary B's exponent at a sufficiently large c. Choose a remaining primary K and N with K^N contained in B^c. For the remaining product P_s, P_s K^N is contained in B^c P_s, which is contained in P_s. The outside length polynomials differ by a constant exponent shift and have identical top forms. A squeeze on every positive rational ray forces the same top form for the middle polynomial. In the full polynomial, after fixing the unused exponent, the degree-n part in the remaining variables comes precisely from terms with unused exponent zero. Polynomial identity therefore proves deletion of unused labels, including repeated labels. With no remaining label, the degree-n>0 coefficient is zero.

Relabelling proves symmetry. Substitution s->ls proves e(I^l,K2,...,Kn)=l e(I,K2,...,Kn). For products use the polynomial with n+1 labels I,J,K2,...,Kn and set the first two variables equal. Only exponent vectors (1,0,1,...,1) and (0,1,1,...,1) contribute to the desired coefficient. The unused-label argument identifies them, giving e(IJ,K2,...,Kn)=e(I,K2,...,Kn)+e(J,K2,...,Kn). Iteration supplies all product and power laws, including unit factors.

If I is contained in J and J is integral over I, homogeneous integral equations make R[Jt] finite over R[It]. Homogeneous module generators of degrees at most c give J^(m+c) contained in I^m: the degree-m+c coefficients lie in I^(m+c-d), contained in I^m. For m>c and any other primary product P_s, I^m P_s is contained in J^m P_s, which is contained in I^(m-c) P_s. The outside length polynomials have identical top forms; squeezing on positive rational rays proves identity of the middle top form. All mixed coefficients agree. Equal integral closures reduce to this case twice through I+J. This is equality of forms, not a coefficient inequality inferred from a nonnegative polynomial; (s-t)^2 illustrates the invalid inference.

For monotonicity suppose J is contained in I and keep K2,...,Kn fixed. Pass algebraically, if needed, to T=R[z]_(mR[z]). This is faithfully flat local with residue field k(z). A finite-length composition series tensors to one with factors k(z), preserving length. Dimension is preserved: an n-generator parameter ideal remains mT-primary, giving dim T<=n by height; flat going-down lifts an n-chain below mT, giving the reverse bound. Every relevant polynomial is unchanged. No boundary base-change assertion is made.

Over the infinite residue field, complete 17.2.2 gives complements of finitely many proper linear subspaces in Kn/mKn for superficial choices for BOTH families (Kn,J,K2,...) and (Kn,I,K2,...). Include avoidance of the current minimal primes. These added subspaces are proper by Nakayama: Kn contained in P+mKn would imply Kn contained in P, impossible for a primary ideal in positive dimension. Their finite intersection has a point. Choose one x and use the SAME quotient for both families. Its dimension is d-1: a quotient prime chain extends strictly down to a minimal prime avoiding x, while lifting a quotient parameter system with x gives the opposite dimension inequality.

Multi-ideal Artin–Rees follows by finite homogeneous generation of the intersection module over the multi-Rees algebra. Together with superficiality, the common primary radical and Krull intersection, complete 17.2.4 gives (P_s:x)=(0:x)+P_(s-e_n) and (0:x) intersect P_(s-e_n)=0 for large exponents. Artin–Rees puts the remainder in the truncated superficial range; intersecting that range over arbitrarily high Kn powers proves the second identity. Consequently (0:x) injects into a finite primary quotient and has finite length. Multiplication by x gives length(R/P_s)-length(R/P_(s-e_n))=length(R/(x,P_s))-length(0:x). For d>1 the last constant does not affect the degree-d-1 coefficient. Reading it gives the superficial reduction for both families on the same quotient, with the zero Kn label removed by the unused-label proof.

Repeat through Kn-1,...,K2 in common successive quotients. All ideal images stay proper primary. The final one-dimensional ring R' gives e_R'(JR') and e_R'(IR'). Inclusion of their powers and the one-variable leading coefficient prove e_R(J,K2,...,Kn)>=e_R(I,K2,...,Kn). For n=1 this proof is direct. The same reductions prove positive mixed multiplicities for proper entries. Units give zero; symmetry supplies every-slot monotonicity, and integral-closure invariance gives closure-order monotonicity. No regular-sequence or CM assumption was inserted.

For an exact sequence of finite modules, multi-ideal Artin–Rees sandwiches P_s M2 intersect M1 between P_s M1 and P_(s-c) M1. The ray squeeze identifies their top forms. The quotient exact sequence proves top-form additivity, with smaller-dimensional modules contributing zero; it does not assert injection after quotienting by P_s.

Finally G331's criterion on ALL X says v(J)>=v(K) iff J is contained in the integral closure of K, with units separate. Equal rational profiles give equal integral closures of cross-powers. The proved laws give equal mixed moments and the correct reversed order for ideal moments. These are mathematical arguments using the disclosed ordinary published dependencies, not finite computations.

notes.summary: Positive bounded measures on the whole G331 D domain, independent of every representation, with uniform weak and actual prescribed-limit decreasing-NET continuity.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves all-support test/function well-definedness, real positive Riesz extension, exact mass and the binomial perturbation bound. Compact directed covers establish representation independence and a continuous-majorant supremum formula. Decreasing bounded D nets converge when their specified limit belongs to D. No increasing closure, nested-net flattening or measure-order inference is used.
notes.text:
Put p=n-1. For rational profiles ui=-v(Ii)/qi, including units, define B_u(v(J))=e(I1,...,Ip,J)/(q1...qp). For p=0 this means e(J), with empty denominator one. N1 proves input-function independence, symmetry, addition, rational homogeneity and ideal-test order.

Every rational ideal-difference test is (v(J)-v(K))/d. Equality with another representation gives v(J^d' K'^d)=v(K^d' J'^d) on every support. Proper products have equal integral closures; equality with a unit forces both products to be units. N1 proves identical functional values, all relation independence and rational linearity. Nonnegative differences give closure inclusion and hence functional positivity; unit cases are immediate or impossible.

Since 1=v(a), positivity on r±f for rational r>||f|| gives |B(f)|<=||f||B(1). G331's dense rational lattice extends B uniquely to real C(X). Real linearity follows by rational scalar approximation. Positivity persists: approximate h>=0 by lattice fj, add rational rj>||h-fj|| tending to zero, and pass B(fj)>=-rjB(1). Compact-Hausdorff Riesz representation gives a unique finite positive Radon measure, of mass e(I1,...,Ip,a)/product(qi).

Write E_J=e(a^[p],J). Comparing inputs in [-M,0] with -M=-Mv(a) gives 0<=B_u(v(J))<=M^p E_J and mass<=M^p e(a). Rational upper bounds handle real M. If two tuples have coordinate distances at most epsilon, use ui-epsilon<=wi and its reverse. Expanding the legitimate negative constant shift gives
|B_u(v(J))-B_w(v(J))| <= [(M+epsilon)^p-M^p] E_J.
Each nonempty subset S of shifted slots contributes a nonnegative term bounded by epsilon^|S| M^(p-|S|) E_J. Set the error to zero for p=0 and interpret M^0=1.

Uniform rational-profile approximation defines C measures independently of approximation. Positivity, mass bounds and Riesz persist. Symmetry, addition and real nonnegative scaling pass to limits. For order, approximants within eta to u<=w satisfy u_app-2eta<=w_app; the shift bound removes the error. Thus the same laws and bound hold on C. Lattice approximation of any continuous test, with the common mass bound, proves uniform weak continuity for arbitrary nets.

For bounded ui in D take ANY actual decreasing C representations gi,alpha_i. All terms already lie in [-M,0] if ui>=-M. On the finite product index set, ideal moments increase and are bounded. Their suprema, and differences of their limits, define a positive bounded lattice functional and hence a Radon measure. Density and mass bounds give weak convergence of the representing measures.

For full representation independence let fi,beta_i be another representation. Fix beta and epsilon>0. The directed open sets {gi,alpha_i<fi,beta_i+epsilon} cover compact X. Finite subcovers and directedness choose a common product index alpha valid everywhere. Then g_alpha-epsilon<=f_beta, so B_fbeta(v(J))<=B_(g_alpha-epsilon)(v(J))<=sup_alpha B_galpha(v(J))+[(M+epsilon)^p-M^p]E_J. Decrease epsilon to zero, take the supremum over beta, and reverse representations. All moments and measures coincide.

The same argument for a fixed C-majorant tuple h>=u gives B_u(v(J))=sup{B_h(v(J)):h in C^p, h>=u}. Such majorants are in [-M,0]. Representing terms give the opposite inequality. This proves ideal-moment order on bounded D, because majorants of a larger tuple form a smaller set. It does not prove order of measures.

Addition, scaling and symmetry on D follow from actual finite product C representations and scalar moment limits. Their sums decrease to the required sums. Hence the negative shift expansion and uniform perturbation bound hold on bounded D too. Uniform convergence inside this established domain implies weak convergence; no increasing closure is assumed.

For actual decreasing-net continuity let ui,lambda in D decrease, with common bound [-M,0], to specified ui in D. Order bounds their increasing moments by the target. For a C-majorant h and epsilon>0, the sets {ui,lambda<hi+epsilon} are open because D functions are upper semicontinuous. They form directed covers. Compactness selects a common lambda, yielding B_h(v(J))<=B_(u_lambda-epsilon)(v(J))<=B_u_lambda(v(J))+[(M+epsilon)^p-M^p]E_J. Take the supremum over lambda, decrease epsilon to zero, and then take the majorant supremum. Every target moment is recovered. Density and mass bounds prove weak convergence on every continuous test. Limit membership in D is a hypothesis; no arbitrary-infimum closure or nested-net flattening is asserted.

notes.summary: Independent supported Cartier intersections: mixed-characteristic thickenings, actual Koszul symmetry, divisor-cycle projection and raw Rees mixed-multiplicity equality.
notes.detailedSummary: Defines local intersection using finite R-length Euler characteristics, retaining all nilpotent Cartier thicknesses and generic-cycle weights. Full symmetry comes from actual supported Koszul complexes. Projection applies to divisor cycles on integral top components before taking Chow quotients. Eventual Rees sections and vanishing prove the diagonal; polynomial equality proves the mixed identity.
notes.text:
On an actual primary blowup Y=Bl_I R use its effective Cartier E_I, ample O(-E_I), reduced dominating components and Cartier order unit from G331. Put p=n-1. For an effective exceptional integral Cartier E, a power of m kills O_E, by coherence and closed-fibre support on a finite affine cover. Its proper cohomology has finite R-length. Define chi_R(E,F)=sum_j(-1)^j length_R H^j(E,F).

For line bundles L1,...,Lr, chi_R(E,O_E tensor product Li^ti) is a polynomial of total degree at most p. Filter O_E by m-powers. Its finitely many graded coherent quotients lie on the proper k-scheme E0 and have support dimension at most p. Tensoring is exact; Euler additivity and complete Stacks 33.45.1 give the polynomial. On these quotients R-length equals k-dimension. This works in mixed characteristic without a coefficient field and retains every nilpotent layer.

Define Q_Y(F1,...,Fp,E) as the coefficient of t1...tp for Li=O(Fi). For p=0 it is length_R H0(E,O_E): the supported proper zero-dimensional scheme is finite over its Artinian base and has no higher cohomology. Complete 33.45.2 applied to the filtration gives
Q_Y(F1,...,Fp,E)=sum_{dim Z=p} length_{O_Y,eta_Z}(O_E,eta_Z) (F1|Z...Fp|Z . Z).
Z is integral reduced and proper over k. The filtration's generic lengths add to the EXACT displayed local length because its residue field is unchanged by the m-quotient. Lower-dimensional supports contribute zero. Fixed twists change no top coefficient.

Polynomial substitution gives symmetry and additivity in the first slots. The exact sequence 0->O_E1(-E2)->O_(E1+E2)->O_E2->0 gives additivity in the effective last slot. The Cartier order unit expresses every integral exceptional F as a difference of effective ones; equality of two differences is equality of effective sums, so extension is well-defined. Extend to real Cartier divisors by multilinearity.

For full symmetry take the ACTUAL complexes K_E=[O(-E)->O] and K_F=[O(-F)->O], using Cartier sections. They resolve O_E and O_F. Their tensor total is unchanged up to sign interchange. Tensor with any line bundle L. Computing its Euler characteristic in the two orders, all within finite-length supported cohomology, gives
chi_R(E,L)-chi_R(E,L(-F))=chi_R(F,L)-chi_R(F,L(-E)).
No regular cut on E or F is required. Put L=O(F)^t O(E)^s product O(Gj)^rj for n-2 further slots. Set t=s=0 and read the r1...r_(n-2) coefficient. The finite differences extract respectively the t and s linear coefficients: total degree at most n-1 excludes higher powers. Thus Q(F,G...,E)=Q(E,G...,F). Effective differences and real linearity prove every transposition; n=1 requires none.

This is supported local degree, not degree on global CH0(Y). On a DVR the parameter divisor has Q=1 although its global Chow class is zero.

For projection take delta(P)=dim R/P. Local catenarity makes this a dimension function; use its standard finite-type transcendence-degree extension. Excellence supplies Stacks 42.7.1's universally catenary hypotheses. Top components have delta-dimension n; closed-fibre dimension is ordinary k-dimension.

A primary refinement or finite normalization is proper birational on every top component. Cartier equations pull back regularly because reduced dominating component generic points avoid the support. At a dimension-p generic point of an exceptional divisor only top components occur: a smaller component dominates its minimal component away from m and cannot contain a dimension-p closed-fibre subvariety. The local ring B is reduced one-dimensional. Embed B into the sum of B/P over minimal primes; the cokernel has finite length. Multiplication by a regular equation g has equal kernel and cokernel lengths on that module. Hence length(B/gB)=sum_P length((B/P)/g(B/P)). The top divisor cycle is therefore the sum of the integral top-component divisor cycles, with reduced generic weights one.

Complete Stacks 42.26.3 gives the ACTUAL cycle equality f_*[f*E]_p=[E]_p, componentwise with function-field degree one. Residue degrees survive. Numerical projection 33.45.7 on proper closed-fibre components then proves Q_Y'(f*F1,...,f*Fn)=Q_Y(F1,...,Fn). Lower-dimensional images contribute zero. Extend by effective differences. No local degree is passed through global Chow rational equivalence.

For the raw diagonal D_I=-E_I, the standard finite Rees algebra gives O(D_I)=O(1). Complete 30.14.3 gives H0(Y,O(qD_I))=I^q for large q; complete 30.16.1(4) gives higher vanishing. The Cartier sequence yields length(I^(q-1)/I^q)=chi_R(E_I,O_EI((q-1)D_I)). Reading degree-p coefficients gives Q(D_I^[p],E_I)=e(I), equivalently -Q(D_I^[n])=e(I), including n=1. No CM, normality or infinite-field assumption is used.

For I1,...,In use a common product blowup. Product ideal powers have divisor sum tj D_Ij. Projection applies the diagonal identity on this model. If H is the top length form, e(product Ij^tj)=n!H(t), by substitution of exponents q tj. Equality of these polynomials on positive integer t, followed by reading t1...tn, proves -Q(D_I1,...,D_In)=e(I1,...,In). This is equality of polynomials, not coefficientwise positivity inferred from domination.

notes.summary: Independent positive geometric atoms and refinement invariance, followed by full real-core comparison using an actual fixed-model section-ideal identity.
notes.detailedSummary: Constructs geometric weights before algebraic comparison and proves their invariance under refinements independently. Generated section ideals satisfy Jq O=O(qL+D0) on the fixed Bl_(I c0), as actual invertible images, supplying maps to Bl_Jq. Common-model polynomial convergence, with a fixed primary uniform error, proves every real-core Cartier moment and presentation independence.
notes.text:
Normalize a common primary model Y, with finite normalization N. Retain its top normal components for degree n; lower components and their points remain in the domain. For each exceptional prime Z of dimension p, its generic ring is a DVR. Set b_Z=ord_Z(a)>0 and nu_Z=ord_Z/b_Z in X, pulled back from its component fraction field with that minimal-component support. For negative-effective real curve-nef D1,...,Dp define independently
mu_geom,Y=sum_Z b_Z (D1|Z...Dp|Z . Z) delta_nu_Z.
The sum is finite. For p=0 the intersection is deg_k Z, including residue degree.

Positivity precedes ideal comparison. G331's qualified real perturbation and rationalization give negative rational ample divisors tending in fixed coefficient spans to each Di. Finite normalization pulls ample bundles to ample bundles, and restriction to Z stays ample. Clearing denominators and complete Stacks 33.45.9 give positive mixed intersections. Their finite coefficient polynomials converge, proving nonnegative real nef weights. This does not use ideal positivity to define weights.

For any exceptional real Cartier F on the model, H_F(nu_Z)=ord_Z(F)/b_Z. Normal divisor cycles and n3 projection give the geometric identity integral H_F dmu_geom,Y=Q_Y(D1,...,Dp,F).

Atomic refinement invariance is proved before moment comparison. The normalization N' of a primary refinement maps properly birationally to N: integral functions defining N lie in the integrally closed local rings of each dominant normal component of N'; properness follows from the closed graph. If Z' maps dominantly to a dimension-p Z, its DVR dominates the DVR of Z in the SAME fraction field. They are equal, because every element is a unit times a uniformizer power and its order sign is preserved. Orders, residue fields, b's and valuations coincide. Apply the actual cycle projection to pulled-back E_I, whose order at Z is positive. It forces exactly one such prime over Z, with degree one. Numerical projection gives the same mixed weight. Every other prime has lower-dimensional image, and its p pulled-back line bundles have intersection zero. Thus the atomic measures agree under refinements independently of algebraic moments. The geometric identity can consequently be tested against Cartier functions on any common refinement.

For comparison fix Y=Bl_I R. G331 gives T=H0(Y,O_Y) finite birational, with T/R supported at m. Choose h killing this quotient and fix ONCE c0=m^(h+1), so c0 T is contained in m AS ELEMENTS OF R. For negative rational ample exceptional L and sufficiently large divisible q, O(qL) is globally generated. Put Fq=H0(Y,O(qL)) contained in T and Jq=c0 Fq contained in R. It is an ideal, proper by c0 T contained in m, and unit away from m by localization and triviality of the divisor there. Hence it is proper primary.

Fix Y'=Bl_(I c0) R, dominating Y and Bl_c0 R; let D0 be the latter's negative divisor. Global generation means equality of the IMAGE of Fq tensor O_Y in O_Y with O(qL). Pullback preserves its surjection; the Cartier inclusion remains injective because its equation is regular on the reduced dominating components. Multiplication by the invertible image of c0 gives the ACTUAL identity
Jq O_Y'=O_Y'(q f*L+D0).
Thus the blowup universal property gives Y'->Bl_Jq R. This is stronger than equality of valuation functions.

For simultaneous Li and qi, n3's raw identity and projection give
e(J1,q1,...,Jn,qn)/(product qi)=-Q_Y'(f*L1+D0/q1,...,f*Ln+D0/qn).
On ALL supports, -v(Jq)/q=H_L-v(c0)/q. The function error is uniform because c0 is PRIMARY. The Cartier side converges by its finite-dimensional polynomial on ONE fixed model.

For real negative curve-nef Di choose rational ample Li,j tending in their fixed coefficient spans to Di and generated divisible qi,j tending to infinity. The SAME c0 and refinement work for every entry and index. Both divisor polynomials and function profiles converge. N2's uniform moment continuity and mass bound for varying continuous tests give integral H_Dn dmu_alg(H_D1,...,H_Dp)=Q_Y(D1,...,Dp,Dn). No intersection convergence was inferred from function convergence alone.

For arbitrary integral exceptional F, choose N so F-NE_I and -NE_I are both negative ample, using G331's order unit and ample twisting. Their difference is F. Test linearity extends the equality to every real exceptional Cartier test. Primary ideal tests live on common primary refinements. The independently proved atomic invariance, geometric identity and comparison identify all their moments. G331's dense ideal-difference lattice therefore proves mu_geom,Y=mu_alg(H_D1,...,H_Dp). This establishes all core presentation and model independence, exact Cartier comparison, and an independently geometric core extended by n2's bounded operator.

notes.summary: Full bounded ordinary open-set locality on all supports, using actual ratio subideals and two justified compact-cover limits.
notes.detailedSummary: Simultaneous invertibility of A,B,A+B gives L+M=O. Strict inequality makes M vanish on the entire integral exceptional prime, so L restricts trivially and atom weights agree. Fixed supported continuous tests extend the identity to C and other bounded D slots. Two successive decreasing limits and uniform convergence within the known domain prove full bounded locality.
notes.text:
Assume p>=1; zero arity is automatic. Synchronize rational denominators and write u=-v(A)/q, w=-v(B)/q. Their maximum is -v(A+B)/q. Take a common primary blowup making A,B,A+B, every other input ideal and a reference primary invertible, then normalize. Unit factors cause no problem; the reference factor ensures a primary model.

Put S=(A+B)O_N. The actual invertible ratio SUBIDEALS L=A O_N/S and M=B O_N/S lie in O_N and satisfy L+M=O_N. At an exceptional prime Z with u(nu_Z)>w(nu_Z), ord_Z(A)<ord_Z(B), so ord_Z(M)>0. Every local generator of M vanishes at the generic point of integral reduced Z and therefore throughout its restriction to Z. The entire map M|Z->O_Z is zero. Restricting L+M=O gives a surjection L|Z->O_Z, hence an isomorphism of line bundles. Thus O(D_A-D_(A+B))|Z is trivial.

In n4's geometric atomic formula, the mixed weights at EVERY atom in the strict set are unchanged when u is replaced by max(u,w). On the same finite divisorial set this proves mu(max(u,w),others)|{u>w}=mu(u,others)|{u>w}. It uses actual ideal images, not only Weil coefficients or moment order.

For C inputs approximate every entry uniformly by rational profiles. A continuous test h with compact support K inside the open strict set has a positive minimum gap there. Accurate approximants preserve strictness on K. The atomic identity and n2 uniform weak continuity pass equality of integrals to C. Now keep the selected u,w in C and represent other bounded D slots by actual decreasing C nets. The strict set and supported test are fixed; n2 decreasing-net continuity extends the identity to those other slots.

Let bounded u,w in D agree on an open U. Fix the other bounded D slots and actual decreasing C representations u_alpha and w_beta, with a common bound. For continuous h with compact support K contained in U and epsilon>0, fix alpha. The directed open sets {w_beta-epsilon<u_alpha} cover K, because the limiting inequality there is w-epsilon=u-epsilon<u_alpha. Compactness selects beta0; its strict set is a FIXED open neighborhood of K remaining strict for every beta>=beta0. The continuous selected-slot identity gives
integral h dmu(max(u_alpha,w_beta-epsilon),others)=integral h dmu(u_alpha,others).

First decrease beta. The selected limit max(u_alpha,w-epsilon) belongs to bounded D by its actual representation or finite-max stability. Then decrease alpha to the known bounded D function max(u,w-epsilon). Apply n2's theorem at each prescribed limit. These two justified limits give integral h dmu(max(u,w-epsilon),others)=integral h dmu(u,others). Interchanging u,w gives the analogous identity.

Both shifted maxima are uniformly within epsilon of the already known max(u,w) in bounded D. Although they increase as epsilon decreases, n2's uniform estimate applies INSIDE the established domain. Let epsilon tend to zero to obtain equality of the integrals for mu(u,others) and mu(w,others).

These tests determine Radon restrictions to U: compact inner regularity and compact-Hausdorff normality supply continuous cutoffs equal to one on compact subsets and supported in U. Thus the restricted measures coincide. Replace slots successively for full mixed locality whenever corresponding tuples agree on U. Every weak limit used a fixed supported continuous test, known domain membership and a finite bound. No increasing closure, nested-net flattening, order of measures or plurifine assertion is used.

notes.summary: Exact one-factor gauge covariance, weighted normalization and full conductor rules, actual curve reference degree, and all reduction and degeneracy conventions.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves the gauge factor v_a(b), reference masses, top-dimensional normalization pushforward with closed residue-field degrees including inseparability, and full conductor quotient behavior. Lower-dimensional points remain with zero top-degree contribution. The zero-arity excellent reduced-curve measure has an actual Cartier comparison and residue-degree example. Empty dimension zero, units, zeros, bottom and nilpotent data are explicit.
notes.text:
For another proper primary b put d(v)=v_a(b)>0 and T(v)=v/d(v). G331 supplies a section homeomorphism and bounded continuous d and inverse. Transport homogeneous inputs by u_b(Tv)=u_a(v)/d(v). Rational profiles have the same ideals and denominators, while tests transform by v_b(J)(Tv)=v_a(J)(v)/d(v). Equality of ideal moments and density prove
mu_b=T_*[d mu_a].
There is ONE d factor, independent of dimension. Uniform C and actual bounded decreasing D continuity extend this identity because input transport preserves these limits, and multiplication by d and compact pushforward are weakly continuous. The new mass is the old moment against v_a(b); rationally it is e(I1,...,Ip,b)/product qi. Successive weights multiply to v_a(c), proving the cocycle. Geometric atom factors transform directly by ord_Z(b)=d(nu_Z) ord_Z(a).

Let S be finite normalization, q its local normal centers, fq=[k(q):k(m)], and rho_q full boundary restriction with gauge aS_q. A regular conductor element kills S/R. Every prime in its support has dimension below n, since its prime chain extends strictly down to a minimal prime not containing that element. N1's top-form additivity gives the same degree-n form for R and S. Artinian decomposition and composition series give length_R(S/PS)=sum_q fq length_Sq(Sq/PSq), for every primary product P. The fq are field dimensions, including inseparable extensions. Comparing degree-n forms yields e_R(I1,...,In)=sum_{dim Sq=n} fq e_Sq(I1Sq,...,InSq).

Testing and extending by the proved continuities gives
mu_R(u)=sum_{dim Sq=n} fq rho_q,* mu_Sq(rho_q* u).
At smaller-dimensional centers the degree-n contribution is ZERO; it is not their own lower-arity intrinsic measure. Those centers, all supports and all potential values remain in the spaces. No points or conductor fibers are deleted and no generic vertical degree is invented.

G331's full quotient says conductor-finite fibers are singletons, while conductor-infinite fibers are exactly equal restrictions through S/conductor -> R/conductor. It supplies positive C,D descent precisely for full-fiber-constant functions. Thus compatible upstairs tuples descend to actual downstairs inputs, and the normalization identity computes the product on the FULL quotient, adding masses on identified fibers. This is a normalization/conductor rule, not full arbitrary finite-map calculus.

For excellent reduced curves n=1,p=0, normal centers are DVRs. Their centered semivaluations are positive multiples of order and have zero support. A regular conductor element has finite value on every branch, giving the finite downstairs branch set nu_q=ord_q/bq, bq=ord_q(a). Define the independent actual Cartier reference measure sum_q fq bq delta_nu_q, of mass e_R(a). Branches mean local normalization centers, including multiple branches of one irreducible component.

For comparison on ANY curve primary model, invertibility of IS gives Spec S->Y. Its graph shows finiteness; its image contains all generic points of reduced Y, so it is surjective and is the normalization. At a closed point put B=O_Y,y, its semilocal normalization Btilde, and C=Btilde/B of finite length. For a regular Cartier equation g the snake sequence is 0->C[g]->B/gB->Btilde/gBtilde->C/gC->0. The kernel and quotient of multiplication on finite-length C have equal lengths. Thus the local Cartier degree equals the sum of DVR orders with residue degrees. Summing and extending by effective differences and real coefficients proves Q_Y(F)=sum_q fq ord_q(F)=integral H_F dmu(). This supplies actual model independence and matches n3–n4. DVR lengths give the ideal moment e_R(J). Zero-arity locality and continuity are constant identities.

Residue weights matter. For ANY finite k subset l of degree d>1, possibly inseparable, R=k+t l[[t]] is a finite algebra over the excellent DVR k[[t]], hence excellent Noetherian. It is local with m=t l[[t]], residue k, fraction field l((t)), finite normalization l[[t]], conductor t l[[t]], generic degree one and residue degree d. For J=t^r l[[t]], a residue basis gives length_R(R/J^N)=1+d(rN-1), so e_R(J)=dr. The m-reference measure is d delta_ord_t. A generic-degree-only weight would be wrong.

For dimension zero the reduction is a field, boundary empty and measure zero; no negative arity or degree-zero multiplicity boundary mass is asserted. For n>=2 a zero input, represented by a unit, annihilates the product; a unit test has zero moment. For p=0 there is no input zero. The tuple -ti v(a) has mass product(ti)e(a), with empty product one. A zero ideal has infinite value and an unbounded bottom profile; it is outside bounded inputs and primary gauges. Unit and zero ideals have no level-one section. A zero scalar means the actual zero function, not formal zero times infinity.

Reduction is essential: k[[t]][epsilon]/(epsilon^2) and k[[t]] have the same boundary but parameter-power lengths 2s and s. Nilpotent generic lengths require extra data. The theorem uses reduced multiplicities, while retaining all actual nilpotent Cartier-thickening lengths on reduced models.

The entire BFJ Section 4 was read. Its Cartier pairing and (4.3), 4.6–4.7 give ideal moments using generic parameter COLENGTH. This equals our polynomial convention in the regular local ring. Consecutive superficial choices and complete 17.3.1 give a joint-reduction parameter tuple. Joint reductions form a nonempty open coefficient set: at a fixed sufficiently large multi-Rees degree the joint-reduction equation is surjectivity of a finite-dimensional multiplication matrix linear in the coefficients; its full-rank condition is open, and Nakayama lifts residue surjectivity. Any joint reduction satisfies such an equation in some degree. Complete 17.4.9 identifies its parameter multiplicity with the polynomial mixed coefficient. Regularity makes the parameter tuple a regular sequence, so parameter multiplicity equals quotient length. Thus generic colength and polynomial multiplicity agree. These CM uses are confined to the smooth comparison.

BFJ 4.7 therefore gives exactly n2's rational moments with the same p=n-1 arity and sign. Scaling, zero/unit conventions and lattice density identify the measures. For C tuples, BFJ 4.4's smooth addition and order give the same negative-constant perturbation estimate and mass bound. Uniform rational approximation identifies their measures with ours.

For bounded D tuples choose any actual decreasing C representations. Their associated nef Weil coefficients decrease at every divisorial valuation to those of the G331-identified limit, hence the product net converges in coefficient topology. The FULL 4.4 proof supplies upper semicontinuity in that topology: strict coefficient inequality below a fixed nef Cartier divisor is an open finite-determination condition; nearly minimizing Cartier majorants can be scaled slightly toward zero to make the inequalities strict. This gives neighborhoods with intersection below any prescribed larger value.

Together with monotonicity, this proves continuity for ANY decreasing coefficient net: intersection values stay above the limit by order, and upper semicontinuity makes their limsup at most the limit. No cofinal sequence is required. Apply this with the fixed ideal Cartier test Z(J); changing sign gives our positive ideal moments. N2's scalar limits, mass bounds and test density identify the whole Radon measures on all semivaluations. The sequence statement 4.8 alone was not promoted to a net theorem.

This is exact smooth OPERATOR specialization. Remark 4.5's essential multiplier approximation, resolution and Rees/Ramanujam intersection foundations remain disclosed smooth dependencies.
